inputs.text: The US has put forward a 15-point ceasefire plan through Pakistan, but Iran’s five counter-conditions—demanding an end to aggression, compensation, and recognition of its sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz—show how far apart the sides remain. A ceasefire that rewards force or gives Tehran greater leverage over a vital passage would not secure lasting peace. Israel is right to remain sceptical and to insist it cannot surrender its ability to defend itself against future threats. Any settlement must protect security and stability, not simply pressure one side to accept Iran’s demands.
